correctness.rationale: With two-dimensional vertex spaces, a nontrivial flag contributes at most one line at each vertex. The incidence condition is a bilinear section of the line bundle of bidegree (1,1), and the map from a two-by-two matrix to that section is a linear isomorphism. Span dimension zero gives the full product, span dimension one gives a smooth or reducible (1,1) divisor, and two or more independent sections have only finite residual intersection unless they share a ruling. Kernel-only and image-only orders reduce to empty, point, or projective-line cases. These underlying complex topological spaces have torsion-free cohomology concentrated in even degree. The inspected exhaustive finite-field verifier is consistent with the classification but is not used as an infinite proof.
